text:
Naturalism holds that philosophy should be continuous with empirical science and that all phenomena are part of the natural world, while positivism is a stricter doctrine claiming that meaningful knowledge comes only from logical or mathematical proofs and empirically verifiable statements. The major difference is that naturalism is a broad metaphysical and methodological commitment to science, whereas positivism is a narrower epistemological criterion for meaning and verification.
